hypothesis.claim: Recent winners keep outperforming recent losers over the next month.
hypothesis.mechanism: Investors underreact to news, so prices adjust with a lag; the trade is hard to arbitrage away because it suffers long, career-threatening drawdowns.
hypothesis.literature: Momentum replicates out-of-sample, internationally and across asset classes, and survives realistic trading costs at scale.

hypothesis.claim: An asset that has risen over the past quarter keeps rising over the next month.
hypothesis.mechanism: Gradual information diffusion plus flows from trend followers; limits to arbitrage keep the drift from being fully priced.
hypothesis.literature: Time-series momentum documented across equities, bonds, commodities and currencies over decades.

hypothesis.claim: Stocks published on the dragon-tiger list underperform over the following week.
hypothesis.mechanism: The after-close disclosure is an attention shock; retail buying pushes price beyond fair value. It is not arbitraged away because A-shares have T+1 settlement, daily price limits and costly shorting.
hypothesis.literature: Attention-driven retail overreaction and short-horizon reversal are documented in retail-dominated markets.

hypothesis.claim: Listings where institutional seats are net buyers outperform listings where they are not.
hypothesis.mechanism: The exchange reveals seat-level flow; institution-only seats proxy informed demand that the wider market has not yet priced.
hypothesis.literature: Informed-flow disclosure predicts returns where the disclosure is mandatory and seat-level.

hypothesis.claim: Stocks where several insiders file open-market sales within days underperform.
hypothesis.mechanism: A single insider sale is diversification noise, but several insiders selling together is costly to fake and plausibly reflects shared private information the market has not priced.
hypothesis.literature: Insider trading is informative; clustered trades are the subset with the strongest documented predictive content.

hypothesis.claim: Altcoins where retail accounts are extremely long underperform over the next week.
hypothesis.mechanism: Retail perp accounts are levered; crowding on one side creates forced liquidations on adverse moves, so extremes revert.
hypothesis.literature: Crowded positioning and funding extremes precede squeezes in perps.

hypothesis.claim: Stocks where several insiders buy on the open market outperform over the next month.
hypothesis.mechanism: Insiders hold private information about their own firm; an open-market purchase costs real money and is legally constrained, so clustered buying is expensive to fake. The market underreacts to the filing.
hypothesis.literature: Insider purchases predict returns while sales are largely diversification noise; clustered trades carry the strongest signal.
hypothesis.universe: All US issuers in SEC Form 345
